CausalChain: Chronic liver disease/inflammation -> increased hepatocyte turnover and DNA damage -> acquisition of aberrant DNA methylation patterns in oncogenes (e.g., TERT, CTNNB1, additional epigenetic markers) -> release of ctDNA with specific methylation signatures into circulation -> detection via integrated liquid biopsy (ctDNA methylation assay + AFP) enhanced by next-generation sequencing and machine learning -> correlation with aggressive tumor behavior and differential response to anti-angiogenic/immunotherapeutic treatments
Hypothesis: An integrated, multi-marker liquid biopsy platform that combines ctDNA methylation profiling of key oncogenic pathways (primarily TERT and CTNNB1, augmented with additional epigenetic markers) with traditional biomarkers such as AFP, and analyzed using cutting-edge next-generation sequencing and machine learning techniques, will enhance the early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and robustly predict patient responses to anti-angiogenic and immunotherapeutic treatments. This approach leverages the biological cascade from chronic liver inflammation-induced DNA damage, the subsequent acquisition of methylation patterns, and their release in ctDNA into the circulation, thereby enabling a more sensitive and specific personalized diagnostic and prognostic tool.
Abstract: We propose an integrated liquid biopsy approach that combines circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation profiling with traditional biomarkers and modern analytical techniques to enhance early detection and treatment stratification in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Specifically, our method focuses on aberrant methylation patterns in key oncogenic pathways such as TERT and CTNNB1, supplemented by additional epigenetic markers to address tumor heterogeneity, and integrates these with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels. Utilizing advanced next-generation sequencing and machine learning algorithms, the platform not only detects ctDNA released as a result of chronic liver inflammation and increased hepatocyte turnover, but also correlates these molecular signatures with aggressive tumor behavior and responses to anti-angiogenic as well as immunotherapeutic treatments. This integrative strategy refines the causal chain from inflammation-induced DNA damage to specific ctDNA signals in circulation, thereby advancing personalized management and prognostication in HCC.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis proposed that ctDNA methylation profiles in TERT and CTNNB1 can independently serve as biomarkers for early HCC detection and predict therapeutic response. The revised hypothesis expands on this by incorporating additional epigenetic markers to counteract tumor heterogeneity and integrating traditional biomarkers (AFP) for enhanced assay performance. Moreover, the new concept leverages contemporary technological advancements—such as next-generation sequencing and machine learning algorithms—to improve sensitivity, specificity, and predictive accuracy, thereby providing a more robust, multi-modal diagnostic platform that directly follows the original causal chain.
